## Vocabulary

Terms this pack was harvested with, grouped by their relation to the concept; counts are units matched / sources. Zero-hit terms are listed under Coverage. On every unit line, `keywords:` names the terms that matched.

- **self**: Standard URI Format (7/2)

## Structure and components

- [statement] The standard MongoDB connection string has the form `mongodb://[username:password@]host1[:port1][,...hostN[:portN]][/[defaultauthdb][?options]]`: credentials are optional, the host list can contain multiple `host[:port]` entries, and the database path and query options are optional. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/connection-string-formats.md · keywords: Standard URI Format · also: https://docs.ovhcloud.com/en/guides/public-cloud/databases/mongodb-connection-strings, https://grafana.com/docs/plugins/grafana-mongodb-datasource/latest/troubleshooting/?plcmt=products-nav

## How it works

- [statement] When a port is omitted from a standard MongoDB URI, the default port is `27017`. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/connection-string-formats.md · keywords: Standard URI Format · also: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/connection-mongodb.html

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] The MongoDB driver specification describes connection strings as URI-style but says their grammar does not conform to RFC 3986 and cannot be parsed by generic URI parsers; applications need a parser that understands MongoDB connection strings. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/connection-string/connection-string-spec.md · keywords: Standard URI Format · also: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3986.html#section-2.1

## Facts and statements

- [statement] The SRV form is `mongodb+srv://[username:password@]host[/[defaultauthdb][?options]]`; it accepts one hostname without an explicit port, then the driver queries DNS SRV records to discover the hosts. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/connection-string-formats.md · keywords: Standard URI Format · also: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/connection-mongodb.html, https://docs.ovhcloud.com/en/guides/public-cloud/databases/mongodb-connection-strings
- [statement] Connection options use `?name=value` query parameters; if options appear without a database path, include `/` between the last host and `?`. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/connection-string-formats.md · keywords: Standard URI Format
- [statement] For portable credentials, percent-encode `$ : / ? # [ ] @` in MongoDB usernames and passwords. RFC 3986 defines a percent-encoded octet as `%` followed by two hexadecimal digits; the MongoDB connection-string specification says drivers should follow RFC 3986 userinfo rules but may accept some reserved characters unencoded for backward compatibility. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/connection-string-formats.md · keywords: Standard URI Format · also: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3986.html#section-2.1, https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/connection-string/connection-string-spec.md, https://grafana.com/docs/plugins/grafana-mongodb-datasource/latest/troubleshooting/?plcmt=products-nav
- [statement] MongoDB's current documentation differs on replica-set seed completeness: the Manual says standard connection strings require all cluster members, while the SDAM specification and current .NET/C# guide describe discovery from a seed list containing one or more members. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/connection-string/ · keywords: Standard URI Format · also: https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/server-discovery-and-monitoring/server-discovery-and-monitoring.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/csharp/current/connect/connection-targets/
